tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2025. Comparative Heibanic. In Helene Fatima Idris, Jan Junglas & Gertrud Schneider-Blum (eds.), Nuba Mountain Language Studies: Contemporary Perspectives, 175-201. Cologne: USB Monographs (Universitaets- und Stadtbibliothek Koeln). doi:10.18716/omp.38.c132.
tone_statements.quote: Proto-Heibanic was almost certainly tonal. Schadeberg (1981a) transcribes high, low and falling tones for some languages. This system is independently confirmed for Shwai in Ali et al. (1998), and for Tira in Watters (1993). Quint (2009) and Kuku (2012) propose a similar two-tone height system for Rere and Laru with an additional rising tone. Moro (Jenks et al. 2024: 89) also has two contrastive tone heights, which are only present on nouns. These occur on vowels, but also on nasals and on /r/ when syllabic.
tone_statements.locator: p. 181, sec. 2.3 'Tones'; cf. p. 178 sec. 2.1 'the vowels and tones are largely guesswork, as they are not apparent from the datasets' and sec. 4.2 'Ko and Warnang remain poorly documented'

sources.note: Group-level only: Proto-Heibanic 'almost certainly tonal'; Schadeberg 1981 transcribed high, low and falling tones for some Heiban languages; two tone heights (+ rising or falling) confirmed for Shwai, Tira, Rere, Laru, Moro; vowels and tones of the proto-language 'largely guesswork'; Ko and Warnang 'remain poorly documented'. Warnang forms are cited with Schadeberg's tone marks (e.g. á-wí, k-íya, ŋʊ́t̪t̪ɔ, uwɔ́y-ú). No Warnang-specific tone inventory.

sources.note: Group-level, second-hand: Heiban tonal systems 'usually involve two registers'; Schadeberg leaves the low register unmarked and GLD adds a grave accent, so the GLD Warnang list is fully tone-marked (H acute, L grave). No Warnang-specific tone statement; nothing on stress.

tone.quote: The phonetic and phonological characteristics of Kordofanian languages are poorly documented and analyzed. The most detailed description (Black and Black 1971) concerns Moro (Heiban group which has an atypically complex system of consonants and consonant clusters. This section présents what I take to be two typical sets of phonological proporties of Kordofanian languages.
